summary:
The Red Planet Survivors is a cooperative, educational web game designed for children aged 7 to 12. Built for 1 to 4 players, the game displays a shared spacecraft cabin on a main screen while players use their smartphones as controllers to assume crew roles and vote on daily decisions.
Based in Jezero Crater, the crew must survive 20 Martian Sols by balancing health, oxygen, energy and base integrity. Each Sol presents a problem grounded in real NASA data and missions. Players assemble a MOXIE generator to produce oxygen, deploy InSight seismic sensors to get early warnings before marsquakes, navigate Earth-Mars communication delays to request mission hints, and react to live solar flare alerts fetched directly from NASA’s DONKI API. 
By transforming open NASA data and authentic planetary engineering into accessible, team-based gameplay, the project irradiates STEM curiosity. It also helps the younger understand the real challenges of human space exploration and the real costs of the decisions taken.
details:
- Overview: A cooperative educational simulation designed for children aged 7 to 12 (1 to 4 players). It transforms complex space exploration and engineering concepts into tangible team decisions, replacing passive learning with active problem-solving under pressure.

- Gameplay Dynamics: The crew must survive 20 Sols (Martian days) by managing 4 shared vital resources (Health, Oxygen, Energy, and Base Integrity). Each player takes on a specialized role (Engineer, Biologist, Medical Officer, or Commander) with exclusive options across an 18-event catalog featuring immediate and delayed consequences (memory effect), real-time voting, and crisis countdowns.

- Scientific Rigor & Live Data: The game connects to official NASA APIs (DONKI for real solar storms from the past 3 days and the Image and Video Library for authentic Jezero Crater backdrops). It integrates mechanics based on real missions, such as the MOXIE oxygen generator (Perseverance), seismometers (InSight), sand dune entrapments and wind-driven solar panel cleaning (Spirit/Opportunity), and anti-radiation probiotics (NASA OSDR), supported by an in-game glossary.

- Tech Stack & Architecture:

- Main Engine (Command Screen): Built in Godot 2D and exported to web technologies.

- Multiplayer Platform: Web app developed with Node.js, WebSockets, and Vue.js to sync mobile devices via room codes (also supports solo play and physical NFC role controller prototypes).

- Objectives & Scalability: Victory requires reaching Sol 20 with positive resources, earning bonus points through 5 secondary objectives (e.g., completing MOXIE to 100% or deploying the seismic network). Its modular architecture is ready to integrate future NASA/JPL APIs (such as Horizons for real radio delays or Mars Rover Photos).

- Red Planet Survivors was developed by Sticky Bit Triggers for the NASA Space Apps Challenge Zaragoza. The main sprites, as well as all the music and sound effects in the game, were created by members of our team. The remaining assets and systems were implemented by the rest of the team, leveraging AI tools responsibly with targeted prompts to streamline the development process.
